authority: Evaluator authored and sealed these additional public cases after the first benchmark. Candidate corrections were withheld before sealing these exact ambitions and gate expectations.

cases.ambition: Une médiathèque veut répartir le temps d’animation entre trois collègues qui peuvent s’associer. Chacun choisit entre une plage tôt ou tard, puis reçoit son propre gain. Quand les trois choisissent tard, les gains sont (6, 6, 6), alors qu’une seule personne tôt ferait gagner 8 à cette personne et 2 aux deux autres. Si deux personnes choisissent tôt, leurs gains sont 1 chacune et la dernière gagne 4. Si les trois sont tôt, chacune gagne 5. Préparez une analyse reproductible des équilibres de Nash purs pour ces trois décisionnaires et clarifiez ce que voudrait dire un accord de coalition. Vérifiez avec un décompte des huit configurations avant d’annoncer une conclusion.
acceptance: Do not route the three-person general-sum game to the qualified two-sided zero-sum allocation tool as a matching capability.
Advance safely through direct enumeration, scoped adaptation, or research/invention of the needed method. Preserve the original three-payoff variable-sum setting.
For a completed solution, identify that all-early is a pure equilibrium and that the three one-early states are other pure equilibria. The all-late state is not a Nash equilibrium.
A coalition agreement requires specifying feasible joint deviations, enforceability and preference comparisons; an informal label does not establish coalition stability.

cases.ambition: Find a reproducible randomized policy for allocating exactly five indivisible exhibition attendants over three stations. The only opposing scheduler privately selects one of two scenarios and its allocation: in A it has 4 attendants and station weights [2, 6, 1]; in B it has 6 attendants and station weights [4, 1, 3]. Our payoff adds the weight if our attendance is higher at a station, subtracts it if theirs is higher, and adds zero for a tie; the opposing payoff is the sign reverse. We want one policy that maximizes the worst expected payoff across hidden scenarios, an exact lower/upper certificate, the relevant computation and an offline run. The scenario is never shown to our policy.
acceptance: Recognize this objective sits exactly within the retained finite zero-sum hidden-scenario allocation capability. Route B with that actual capability or calculate and independently verify the same finite instance directly.
Preserve integer equality budgets, all six weights, two scenarios, zero ties, and one shared policy.
Do not assert completed computation without a feasible probability certificate and independently recomputed matching bounds.
A reproducible scope-faithful invocation plus correct supported inputs counts as actionable progress.
